mechanism_claims.claim_text: Selected bactenecin derivatives increased outer-membrane permeability of Escherichia coli UB1005 in an NPN uptake assay.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure-level dose curves were not numerically tabulated in local XML/PDF; qualitative ordering is source-supported.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The selected peptides permeabilized the inner membrane of Escherichia coli UB1005 at 1 × MIC in an ONPG uptake assay.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Source supports time-dependent permeabilization and rank order; exact curve points are figure-only.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The selected peptides depolarized the Escherichia coli UB1005 cytoplasmic membrane at 1 × MIC in a diSC3-5 fluorescence assay.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Source supports relative depolarization over 300 s; exact curve points are figure-only.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: PI flow cytometry showed cytoplasmic membrane integrity loss in Escherichia coli ATCC25922 at 1 × MIC.
mechanism_claims.limitations: PI percentages are extractable from prose; per-panel raw flow histograms are figure-only.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM/TEM images showed membrane roughening, fracture, holes, and intracellular content leakage after 1 × MIC treatment.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Morphology is qualitative; no numeric lesion counts are reported in local XML/PDF.

summary: Primary source supports a membrane-disruption mechanism through permeability, depolarization, PI flow cytometry, and electron microscopy assays; figure-only quantitative curves are not over-normalized.
